name: Cavity and waveguide modes become photon modes
summary: To quantize the field, expand it in the classical normal modes of the cavity or waveguide (Helmholtz solutions obeying the boundary conditions) and promote each mode amplitude to a harmonic-oscillator operator. Mode shapes, mode volumes and dispersion carry over unchanged.

name: Field momentum and radiation pressure in optomechanics
summary: The momentum carried by electromagnetic fields (Poynting vector, Maxwell stress tensor) pushes on a reflector with radiation pressure 2P/c. In a cavity this force scales with the intracavity photon number, which gives the optomechanical coupling used to cool, squeeze and entangle mechanical motion.
map: \mathbf g=\epsilon_0\mathbf E\times\mathbf B,\ F=\frac{2P}{c}\to\hat F=\hbar G\hat a^\dagger\hat a,\ G=\frac{\omega_c}{L},\ g_0=Gx_{\rm zpf}
sources: Aspelmeyer, Kippenberg & Marquardt (2014). "Cavity optomechanics". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 86, 1391. [arXiv:1303.0733](https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.0733)

name: Aharonov–Bohm phase as holonomy of the potential
summary: The vector potential is a U(1) connection: a charge that encircles a flux picks up the phase q∮A·dl/ħ even where B=0. Berry's phase is the same holonomy, taken for a connection on parameter space.
map: \varphi_{AB}=\frac{q}{\hbar}\oint\mathbf A\cdot d\mathbf l=\frac{q\Phi}{\hbar}\ \leftrightarrow\ \gamma_B=\oint\mathcal A\cdot d\mathbf R,\ \mathcal A=i\langle n|\nabla_R n\rangle
sources: Aharonov & Bohm (1959). "Significance of Electromagnetic Potentials in the Quantum Theory". *Phys. Rev.* 115, 485. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.115.485](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.115.485)
Berry (1984). "Quantal phase factors accompanying adiabatic changes". *Proc. R. Soc. A* 392, 45. [doi:10.1098/rspa.1984.0023](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1984.0023)

name: Spin–orbit coupling from field transformations
summary: An electron moving through an atom's electric field sees a magnetic field B'=−v×E/c² in its rest frame, which couples to its spin. Relativistic Thomas precession halves the naive result, giving the fine-structure term that the Dirac equation yields directly.
sources: Dirac (1928). "The quantum theory of the electron". *Proc. R. Soc. A* 117, 610. [doi:10.1098/rspa.1928.0023](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1928.0023)

name: Earnshaw's theorem and the RF Paul trap
summary: Laplace's equation rules out a static 3D potential minimum for a charge (Earnshaw's theorem). Ion traps therefore use an oscillating quadrupole whose time-averaged ponderomotive pseudopotential confines the ion, and designing the electrodes is an electrostatic boundary-value problem.
sources: Cirac & Zoller (1995). "Quantum Computations with Cold Trapped Ions". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 74, 4091. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.74.4091](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.74.4091)

name: Lorentz oscillator and quantum oscillator strengths
summary: The classical Lorentz model of a bound electron gives the dielectric function and Rayleigh's ω^4 law. Quantum mechanics keeps its form, placing resonances at transition frequencies weighted by oscillator strengths that obey the Thomas–Reiche–Kuhn sum rule. Kramers–Heisenberg dispersion theory led directly to Heisenberg's matrix mechanics.
sources: Heisenberg (1925). "Über quantentheoretische Umdeutung kinematischer und mechanischer Beziehungen". *Z. Phys.* 33, 879. [doi:10.1007/BF01328377](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01328377)

name: Multipole order sets atomic selection rules
summary: Expanding the atom–field coupling in multipoles gives E1, M1, E2… transitions. Their angular-momentum and parity selection rules follow from each multipole's spherical-tensor rank, and each higher order is suppressed by about (ka)^2. The resulting narrow 'forbidden' lines serve as clock transitions.

name: Lasers as the enabling toolkit of AMO physics
summary: Narrow-linewidth, tunable, stabilized lasers made laser cooling, optical trapping, precision spectroscopy and coherent control of atoms possible. In return, atomic references stabilize laser frequencies.
sources: Schawlow & Townes (1958). "Infrared and Optical Masers". *Phys. Rev.* 112, 1940. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.112.1940](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.112.1940)
Ashkin (1970). "Acceleration and Trapping of Particles by Radiation Pressure". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 24, 156. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.24.156](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.24.156)

name: Photonic devices as quantum-optical hardware
summary: The laser is itself a quantum-optical system: spontaneous-emission noise sets its Schawlow–Townes linewidth, and above threshold it emits near-coherent light. Photonic components (nonlinear crystals, waveguides, cavities) are the building blocks of quantum light sources and circuits.
sources: Schawlow & Townes (1958). "Infrared and Optical Masers". *Phys. Rev.* 112, 1940. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.112.1940](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.112.1940)
Glauber (1963). "The Quantum Theory of Optical Coherence". *Phys. Rev.* 130, 2529. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.130.2529](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.130.2529)

name: Integrated linear optics as photonic quantum processors
summary: Classical integrated-photonics parts (directional couplers, thermo-optic phase shifters, Mach–Zehnder meshes that realize any unitary) become photonic qubit gates. They underpin linear-optical (KLM) and fusion-based architectures and boson-sampling machines.
map: \hat a^\dagger_{{\rm out},i}=\sum_jU_{ij}\hat a^\dagger_{{\rm in},j},\ U\in U(N)\ \text{from }N(N-1)/2\ \text{MZIs}
sources: Knill, Laflamme & Milburn (2001). "A scheme for efficient quantum computation with linear optics". *Nature* 409, 46. [doi:10.1038/35051009](https://doi.org/10.1038/35051009)

name: Telecom fibre and photonic chips for QKD
summary: Quantum key distribution and entanglement distribution run on low-loss 1550 nm telecom fibre with integrated transmitters and receivers. Fibre transmission falls exponentially with distance, which caps repeaterless key rates and motivates quantum repeaters.
sources: Kao & Hockham (1966). "Dielectric-fibre surface waveguides for optical frequencies". *Proc. IEE* 113, 1151. [doi:10.1049/piee.1966.0189](https://doi.org/10.1049/piee.1966.0189)
Ekert (1991). "Quantum cryptography based on Bell's theorem". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 67, 661. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.67.661](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.67.661)

name: Frequency combs and stabilized lasers for optical clocks
summary: A mode-locked laser's pulse train is a comb of exactly spaced lines that links optical clock transitions to countable microwave frequencies. Pound–Drever–Hall locking to ultrastable cavities gives the sub-hertz-linewidth lasers that interrogate lattice and ion clocks.
sources: Ludlow et al. (2015). "Optical atomic clocks". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 87, 637. [arXiv:1407.3493](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.3493)

name: Laser radiation pressure: Doppler cooling and traps
summary: A narrow-linewidth laser tuned below resonance exerts a velocity-dependent scattering force that Doppler-cools atoms to T_D=ħΓ/2k_B. Intense far-detuned beams instead give conservative dipole potentials, the basis of optical traps and tweezers.
sources: Ashkin (1970). "Acceleration and Trapping of Particles by Radiation Pressure". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 24, 156. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.24.156](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.24.156)
Raab et al. (1987). "Trapping of Neutral Sodium Atoms with Radiation Pressure". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 59, 2631. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.59.2631](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.59.2631)

name: Optical resonators: laser cavity to strong coupling
summary: The Fabry–Pérot resonator that gives a laser its feedback becomes, at small mode volume and high finesse, a cavity where one atom and one photon exchange energy faster than either decays. The same Q/V figure of merit sets the Purcell factor.
sources: Jaynes & Cummings (1963). "Comparison of quantum and semiclassical radiation theories with application to the beam maser". *Proc. IEEE* 51, 89. [doi:10.1109/PROC.1963.1664](https://doi.org/10.1109/PROC.1963.1664)

name: Einstein A/B and laser photon statistics
summary: Einstein's A/B ratio, derived from Planck's law, says spontaneous emission is stimulated emission driven by the vacuum's one photon per mode. Below threshold a laser emits thermal-like light with g^(2)(0)=2; above threshold its output is near-Poissonian coherent light with g^(2)(0)→1.
sources: Glauber (1963). "The Quantum Theory of Optical Coherence". *Phys. Rev.* 130, 2529. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.130.2529](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.130.2529)

name: Superconducting circuits as microwave metamaterials
summary: Josephson-junction arrays and high-kinetic-inductance lines are lumped-element metamaterials with engineered dispersion. Dispersion engineering (band gaps, resonant phase matching) underlies Josephson travelling-wave parametric amplifiers, Purcell filters and band-gap waveguides coupled to transmons.
map: \epsilon,\mu\to C_\ell,\ L_\ell(\Phi)\ \text{per unit length},\ v_p=1/\sqrt{L_\ell C_\ell},\ L_J=\frac{\Phi_0}{2\pi I_c\cos\varphi}

name: Photonic band gaps and nanocavities in cavity QED
summary: A photonic band gap suppresses spontaneous emission by removing optical modes. Photonic-crystal and plasmonic nanocavities with tiny mode volumes enhance it (Purcell effect) and reach strong coupling with single quantum dots or molecules: cavity QED in engineered media.
map: \Gamma\propto|\mathbf d\cdot\mathbf E|^2\rho_{\rm LDOS}(\omega),\ \ g\propto V^{-1/2},\ \ F_P\propto Q/V
sources: Yablonovitch (1987). "Inhibited Spontaneous Emission in Solid-State Physics and Electronics". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 58, 2059. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.58.2059](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.58.2059)

name: Kerr NLSE in fibres ↔ Gross–Pitaevskii equation
summary: Pulses in a Kerr fibre and a BEC's mean-field dynamics obey the same cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation. Bright and dark solitons, modulational instability, self-focusing collapse and four-wave mixing all have matter-wave counterparts, and 'fluids of light' show superfluid-like flow.
breaks: In fibres the evolution variable is distance and 'space' is retarded time. BECs have traps, quantum depletion and true 3D collapse, and optical fluids are driven-dissipative rather than in equilibrium.

name: Josephson junctions as microwave Kerr nonlinearities
summary: The Josephson cosine potential is a lossless microwave nonlinearity: expanded about its minimum, its quartic Kerr term makes the transmon an anharmonic oscillator. Pumped junctions work as parametric amplifiers and frequency converters, carrying four-wave mixing, phase matching and squeezing over to circuits.
sources: Koch et al. (2007). "Charge-insensitive qubit design derived from the Cooper pair box". *Phys. Rev. A* 76, 042319. [arXiv:cond-mat/0703002](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0703002)

name: SPDC: heralded single photons and entangled pairs
summary: Spontaneous parametric down-conversion is vacuum-seeded χ(2) difference-frequency generation: a pump photon splits into signal and idler photons, with phase matching enforcing energy and momentum conservation. Detecting one photon heralds the other, and type-II phase matching yields polarization-entangled pairs.
map: \omega_p=\omega_s+\omega_i,\ \mathbf k_p=\mathbf k_s+\mathbf k_i\,(+2\pi/\Lambda\ \text{QPM}),\ H\propto\chi^{(2)}\hat a_p\hat a_s^\dagger\hat a_i^\dagger+\text{h.c.}
sources: Hong, Ou & Mandel (1987). "Measurement of subpicosecond time intervals between two photons by interference". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 59, 2044. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.59.2044](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.59.2044)

name: Parametric down-conversion as a squeezing source
summary: A degenerate χ(2) parametric amplifier (an OPO below threshold) produces squeezed vacuum through its two-photon Hamiltonian, and Kerr χ(3) media also squeeze. These sources are now injected into gravitational-wave interferometers.
map: H=\frac{i\hbar\kappa}{2}(\hat a^{\dagger2}-\hat a^2)\Rightarrow\Delta X_{\rm sq}=\tfrac12e^{-r},\ \Delta X_{\rm anti}=\tfrac12e^{r},\ r=\kappa t
sources: Caves (1981). "Quantum-mechanical noise in an interferometer". *Phys. Rev. D* 23, 1693. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.23.1693](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.23.1693)

name: Helical waveguide arrays as Floquet topological insulators
summary: In coupled waveguide arrays the paraxial equation makes propagation distance z act as time. Helically modulated waveguides therefore form a periodically driven lattice whose Floquet bands carry (anomalous) topology and chiral edge states, Floquet engineering demonstrated first with light.
sources: Ozawa et al. (2019). "Topological photonics". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 91, 015006. [arXiv:1802.04173](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.04173)

name: Gain/loss photonics: PT symmetry and exceptional points
summary: Optical lattices and resonators with engineered gain and loss are the main experimental platform for PT-symmetric Hamiltonians, exceptional points, the non-Hermitian skin effect and topological lasers. There the paraxial wave equation plays the role of a Schrödinger equation with a complex potential.
sources: Bender & Boettcher (1998). "Real Spectra in Non-Hermitian Hamiltonians Having PT Symmetry". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 80, 5243. [arXiv:physics/9712001](https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/9712001)
Ozawa et al. (2019). "Topological photonics". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 91, 015006. [arXiv:1802.04173](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.04173)

name: Berry curvature and Chern numbers of photonic bands
summary: Bloch modes of photonic crystals carry the same Berry connection and curvature as electronic bands. Breaking time reversal with magneto-optic media gives nonzero Chern numbers and chiral, backscattering-immune edge modes.
map: \mathcal A_n=i\langle u_{n\mathbf k}|\nabla_{\mathbf k}u_{n\mathbf k}\rangle_\epsilon,\ C=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{\rm BZ}\Omega\,d^2k\in\mathbb Z,\ N_{\rm edge}=\Delta C
breaks: The photonic inner product is ε-weighted, and with no Fermi level there is no quantized Hall conductance, only bulk–edge mode counting.
sources: Berry (1984). "Quantal phase factors accompanying adiabatic changes". *Proc. R. Soc. A* 392, 45. [doi:10.1098/rspa.1984.0023](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1984.0023)
Ozawa et al. (2019). "Topological photonics". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 91, 015006. [arXiv:1802.04173](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.04173)

name: High-harmonic generation as a sum over quantum orbits
summary: The three-step recollision model of HHG is a semiclassical evaluation of the strong-field path integral. Saddle points of the action give complex 'quantum orbits' whose classical return energy produces the I_p+3.17U_p cutoff, and the imaginary part of the ionization time encodes tunnelling.
sources: Krausz & Ivanov (2009). "Attosecond physics". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 81, 163. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.81.163](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.81.163)
Paul et al. (2001). "Observation of a Train of Attosecond Pulses from High Harmonic Generation". *Science* 292, 1689. [doi:10.1126/science.1059413](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1059413)

name: Cherenkov emission and the Landau critical velocity
summary: A source moving faster than the phase velocity of a medium's waves radiates them (Cherenkov emission). The Landau criterion for superfluidity is the same kinematic condition for emitting Bogoliubov excitations, so an obstacle dragged through a BEC faster than v_c≈c_s leaves a Cherenkov-like phonon wake.
breaks: The Bogoliubov dispersion is nonlinear, so the threshold is min ε/p rather than a constant phase velocity and the wake is not a simple cone. In practice, vortex nucleation sets a lower critical velocity.

name: Larmor dipole power ↔ Einstein A coefficient
summary: An atomic transition's spontaneous-emission rate equals the classical Larmor power of a dipole oscillating with amplitude 2|d_12|, divided by ħω. This is the correspondence principle at its sharpest, and it fixes natural linewidths and lifetimes.
breaks: A classical dipole decays continuously; quantum emission happens in discrete jumps, needs vacuum fluctuations to start from an energy eigenstate, and never occurs from the ground state.

name: Purcell effect: classical dipole power = quantum rate
summary: At weak coupling, any photonic environment changes a quantum emitter's decay rate by exactly the factor it changes a classical dipole's radiated power. Both are set by the local density of optical states (the dyadic Green's function), which guides nanoantenna and cavity design for bright single-photon sources.
map: \frac{\Gamma}{\Gamma_0}=\frac{P}{P_0}=\frac{6\pi c}{\omega}\,\hat{\mathbf n}\cdot\mathrm{Im}\,\mathbf G(\mathbf r_0,\mathbf r_0;\omega)\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}
breaks: Fails at strong coupling (vacuum Rabi splitting, non-exponential decay) and says nothing about photon statistics.

name: Larmor collapse of the classical atom
summary: By the Larmor formula, a classical electron orbiting a proton radiates and spirals in within about 10^-11 s. This instability of Rutherford's atom forced Bohr's quantization, and it is resolved by the stationary states of the quantum hydrogen atom.

name: Mie partial waves, optical theorem, Born approximation
summary: Mie theory expands the scattered field in vector spherical harmonics with coefficients a_n, b_n, exactly as quantum partial-wave analysis uses phase shifts δ_l. The optical theorem began as optical extinction, and Rayleigh–Gans scattering is the first Born approximation.
breaks: Light is a vector field: there are two multipole families (TE and TM) and no monopole term, so the Mie sum starts at n=1.
sources: Mie (1908). "Beiträge zur Optik trüber Medien, speziell kolloidaler Metallösungen". *Ann. Phys.* 330, 377. [doi:10.1002/andp.19083300302](https://doi.org/10.1002/andp.19083300302)
Born (1926). "Zur Quantenmechanik der Stoßvorgänge". *Z. Phys.* 37, 863. [doi:10.1007/BF01397477](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01397477)

name: Thermodynamics extended to quantum systems
summary: Quantum thermodynamics keeps the laws (energy balance, Clausius inequality, Carnot bound) but defines work and heat for density matrices and open-system maps. Coherence and entanglement act as additional resources or costs.
map: dU=\mathrm{Tr}(\dot\rho H)+\mathrm{Tr}(\rho\dot H)=\dot Q+\dot W;\ \Delta S\ge\beta Q

name: Quantum heat engines and refrigerators
summary: Otto, Carnot and absorption cycles run with qubits, oscillators and spins as working media; the Carnot bound survives with thermal baths. Non-thermal (squeezed, coherent) reservoirs can exceed η_C because they are not heat in the classical sense.

name: Third law and second laws in the quantum regime
summary: The unattainability principle has been derived and quantified for quantum systems: cooling time diverges as T→0, with a bound set by the bath's density of states. For small systems the second law splits into a family of single-shot conditions.
sources: Masanes & Oppenheim (2017). "A general derivation and quantification of the third law of thermodynamics". *Nat. Commun.* 8, 14538. [arXiv:1412.3828](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.3828)

name: Anderson localization and MBL in cold atoms
summary: Optical speckle and quasiperiodic lattices made matter-wave Anderson localization directly visible (exponential density profiles), and interacting fermions in quasiperiodic lattices kept memory of an initial density wave, the first MBL signature.
sources: Billy et al. (2008). "Direct observation of Anderson localization of matter waves in a controlled disorder". *Nature* 453, 891. [arXiv:0804.1621](https://arxiv.org/abs/0804.1621)
Schreiber et al. (2015). "Observation of many-body localization of interacting fermions in a quasirandom optical lattice". *Science* 349, 842. [arXiv:1501.05661](https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.05661)

name: MBL-protected discrete time crystals
summary: Generic periodically driven many-body systems heat to infinite temperature. MBL prevents this and allows period-doubled spatiotemporal order, the discrete time crystal, which is stable to perturbations of the drive.
sources: Else, Bauer & Nayak (2016). "Floquet Time Crystals". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 117, 090402. [arXiv:1603.08001](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.08001)

name: Hatano–Nelson: non-Hermitian localization from flux lines
summary: Non-Hermitian quantum mechanics as a field grew from the statistical mechanics of flux lines pinned by columnar defects in superconductors. An imaginary vector potential (tilted field) delocalizes Anderson states, the first non-Hermitian localization transition and the ancestor of the non-Hermitian skin effect.
sources: Hatano & Nelson (1996). "Localization Transitions in Non-Hermitian Quantum Mechanics". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 77, 570. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.77.570](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.77.570)

name: Level statistics: Poisson vs Wigner–Dyson
summary: Spectral statistics diagnose both Anderson/MB localization and quantum chaos: localized states give Poisson level spacings, and ergodic or extended states give random-matrix (GOE) repulsion. The ratio ⟨r⟩ is the standard order parameter for the MBL transition.
sources: Oganesyan & Huse (2007). "Localization of interacting fermions at high temperature". *Phys. Rev. B* 75, 155111. [arXiv:cond-mat/0610854](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0610854)

name: Many-body localization as ETH failure
summary: MBL is the main known mechanism by which an interacting, non-integrable quantum system violates ETH. Eigenstates have area-law entanglement and Poisson level statistics, and local memory survives forever.
sources: Nandkishore & Huse (2015). "Many-Body Localization and Thermalization in Quantum Statistical Mechanics". *Annu. Rev. Condens. Matter Phys.* 6, 15. [arXiv:1404.0686](https://arxiv.org/abs/1404.0686)

Basko, Aleiner & Altshuler (2006). "Metal–insulator transition in a weakly interacting many-electron system with localized single-particle states". *Ann. Phys.* 321, 1126. [arXiv:cond-mat/0506617](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0506617)

name: Measurement-induced transitions and percolation
summary: In monitored random circuits, the zeroth Rényi entanglement entropy maps exactly onto a minimal cut through a percolation cluster. The measurement-induced volume-to-area-law transition therefore becomes classical percolation in this limit, and higher Rényi entropies flow to distinct non-percolation classes.
sources: Skinner, Ruhman & Nahum (2019). "Measurement-Induced Phase Transitions in the Dynamics of Entanglement". *Phys. Rev. X* 9, 031009. [arXiv:1808.05953](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05953)

name: Percolation thresholds for photonic cluster states
summary: Probabilistic fusion gates build random lattices of entangled photons, and a cluster state usable for universal measurement-based computation exists only above the bond-percolation threshold. Renormalizing the percolated lattice yields a regular resource, so loss tolerance is a percolation problem.
sources: Kieling, Rudolph & Eisert (2007). "Percolation, Renormalization, and Quantum Computing with Nondeterministic Gates". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 99, 130501. [arXiv:quant-ph/0611140](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0611140)

name: SYK model began as a quantum spin glass
summary: The Sachdev–Ye random all-to-all Heisenberg magnet, introduced to study a quantum spin-glass/spin-liquid transition, became (as SYK) the canonical maximally chaotic quantum system. Random couplings, large-N and replica tools come straight from spin-glass theory.
sources: Sachdev & Ye (1993). "Gapless spin-fluid ground state in a random quantum Heisenberg magnet". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 70, 3339. [arXiv:cond-mat/9212030](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9212030)

name: Spin-glass ground states and quantum annealing
summary: NP-hard optimization problems map onto spin-glass (Ising) ground-state searches. Quantum annealing replaces thermal fluctuations with a transverse field, and RSB landscapes and small gaps at first-order transitions limit its speedup.
sources: Kadowaki & Nishimori (1998). "Quantum annealing in the transverse Ising model". *Phys. Rev. E* 58, 5355. [arXiv:cond-mat/9804280](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9804280)
Lucas (2014). "Ising formulations of many NP problems". *Front. Phys.* 2, 5. [arXiv:1302.5843](https://arxiv.org/abs/1302.5843)

name: Toric-code threshold as a random-bond Ising transition
summary: Optimal decoding of the surface code under independent bit-flip noise maps onto the 2D random-bond Ising model on the Nishimori line. The error threshold p_c≈10.9% is that model's ordering transition, and spin-glass replica tools now analyze qLDPC codes.
sources: Dennis et al. (2002). "Topological quantum memory". *J. Math. Phys.* 43, 4452. [arXiv:quant-ph/0110143](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0110143)

name: Quantum gases as statistical-mechanics laboratories
summary: Dilute ultracold Bose and Fermi gases realize textbook equilibrium statistical mechanics (ideal and weakly interacting BE/FD gases, BEC, degenerate Fermi pressure) with tunable interactions and traps.
sources: Dalfovo et al. (1998). "Theory of Bose-Einstein condensation in trapped gases". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 71, 463. [arXiv:cond-mat/9806038](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9806038)

name: Why isolated quantum systems look thermal
summary: ETH supplies the quantum-mechanical foundation that equilibrium statistical mechanics assumes. Individual energy eigenstates already give microcanonical expectation values for few-body observables, so ergodicity is not needed.
sources: D'Alessio et al. (2016). "From quantum chaos and eigenstate thermalization to statistical mechanics and thermodynamics". *Adv. Phys.* 65, 239. [arXiv:1509.06411](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.06411)

name: Negative absolute temperature in optical lattices
summary: A Bose–Hubbard gas with an upper-bounded energy spectrum (via band truncation and attractive U) was prepared at negative temperature, the textbook two-level-system case realized for motional degrees of freedom. It also revived the Gibbs-vs-Boltzmann entropy debate.
sources: Braun et al. (2013). "Negative Absolute Temperature for Motional Degrees of Freedom". *Science* 339, 52. [arXiv:1211.0545](https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.0545)

name: Ensemble equivalence from eigenstate thermalization
summary: Under ETH the diagonal ensemble of a quench equals the microcanonical ensemble, which by ensemble equivalence equals the canonical one for local observables. Integrable systems need a generalized Gibbs ensemble instead.
sources: D'Alessio et al. (2016). "From quantum chaos and eigenstate thermalization to statistical mechanics and thermodynamics". *Adv. Phys.* 65, 239. [arXiv:1509.06411](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.06411)

name: Canonical typicality from entanglement
summary: For almost every pure state of a large system plus bath with fixed total energy, the reduced state of a small subsystem is close to canonical. Entanglement with the bath, not ensemble averaging over ignorance, explains the canonical ensemble.
sources: Popescu, Short & Winter (2006). "Entanglement and the foundations of statistical mechanics". *Nat. Phys.* 2, 754. [arXiv:quant-ph/0511225](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0511225)

name: Wick rotation: Z as an imaginary-time path integral
summary: Tr e^{-βH} is a Feynman path integral over paths periodic in imaginary time with period βħ. Quantum statistical mechanics in d dimensions is therefore classical statistical mechanics of polymers or fields in d+1 dimensions, which is the basis of path-integral Monte Carlo for helium.
sources: Feynman (1953). "Atomic Theory of the λ Transition in Helium". *Phys. Rev.* 91, 1291. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.91.1291](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.91.1291)

name: Landauer, demons and quantum resource theories
summary: Landauer erasure, Szilard engines and Maxwell demons generalize to qubits, where entanglement and coherence change the bookkeeping (negative conditional entropy can allow work extraction during erasure). Resource theories of athermality replace the free energy with a family of Rényi free energies for single-shot processes.
sources: Parrondo, Horowitz & Sagawa (2015). "Thermodynamics of information". *Nat. Phys.* 11, 131. [doi:10.1038/nphys3230](https://doi.org/10.1038/nphys3230)

name: Thermal entropy as eigenstate entanglement entropy
summary: In a thermalizing pure state, a subsystem's entanglement entropy equals the thermodynamic entropy at the effective temperature (volume law). This was measured in a quantum gas microscope, where entanglement entropy became thermal entropy.
sources: Kaufman et al. (2016). "Quantum thermalization through entanglement in an isolated many-body system". *Science* 353, 794. [arXiv:1603.04409](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.04409)

name: Information is physical: qubits and thermodynamics
summary: Quantum information inherits Shannon theory and Landauer's principle. Reversible unitary gates dissipate nothing in principle, but resetting ancillas and measurement records costs at least k_BT ln2 per bit.
sources: Landauer (1961). "Irreversibility and Heat Generation in the Computing Process". *IBM J. Res. Dev.* 5, 183. [doi:10.1147/rd.53.0183](https://doi.org/10.1147/rd.53.0183)

name: Shannon, von Neumann and entanglement entropy
summary: The von Neumann entropy of a reduced density matrix is the quantum Shannon entropy and measures entanglement for pure bipartite states. It reduces to Gibbs entropy for thermal states.

name: Shannon theory in quantum key distribution
summary: QKD security and channel capacities are written in entropies inherited from Shannon. The BB84 key rate uses the binary entropy h(Q), and the Holevo bound and quantum relative entropy generalize classical mutual information.

name: Integrability, GGE and the quantum Newton's cradle
summary: Bethe-ansatz-integrable systems such as the Lieb–Liniger gas have extensively many conserved charges and do not thermalize to a Gibbs state. Trapped 1D Bose gases (the quantum Newton's cradle, Tonks–Girardeau gases) showed this, and the steady state is a generalized Gibbs ensemble.
sources: Kinoshita, Wenger & Weiss (2006). "A quantum Newton's cradle". *Nature* 440, 900. [doi:10.1038/nature04693](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature04693)
Kinoshita, Wenger & Weiss (2004). "Observation of a One-Dimensional Tonks-Girardeau Gas". *Science* 305, 1125. [doi:10.1126/science.1100700](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1100700)

Lieb & Liniger (1963). "Exact Analysis of an Interacting Bose Gas. I. The General Solution and the Ground State". *Phys. Rev.* 130, 1605. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.130.1605](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.130.1605)

name: Blackbody radiation shift in optical clocks
summary: The ambient Planck field Stark-shifts clock transitions by an amount ∝T⁴. It is a leading systematic of optical lattice clocks and has driven cryogenic clocks with fractional BBR uncertainty near 10^{-20}.
sources: Hassan et al. (2025). "Cryogenic Optical Lattice Clock with 1.7×10^{-20} Blackbody Radiation Stark Uncertainty". [arXiv:2506.05304](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.05304)

name: Bose–Einstein condensation from quantum statistics to atoms
summary: The BEC critical temperature from Bose–Einstein statistics, nλ³=ζ(3/2), was realized in 1995 in dilute alkali gases. Trapped gases modify the density of states (T_c∝N^{1/3}ω) but test the same counting.
sources: Dalfovo et al. (1998). "Theory of Bose-Einstein condensation in trapped gases". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 71, 463. [arXiv:cond-mat/9806038](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9806038)

name: Indistinguishability and the symmetrization postulate
summary: Bose and Fermi statistics follow from the symmetrization postulate for identical particles, and Gibbs' 1/N! (the resolution of the mixing paradox) is its classical limit. Thermal states are density operators ρ=e^{-βH}/Z in the postulates' formalism.

name: Thermal light: Bose–Einstein photon statistics
summary: A single mode of blackbody radiation has a Bose–Einstein (geometric) photon-number distribution with variance n̄²+n̄, which is the origin of Hanbury Brown–Twiss bunching g²(0)=2. Coherent states are Poissonian, so photon statistics distinguish thermal from laser light.
sources: Glauber (1963). "Coherent and Incoherent States of the Radiation Field". *Phys. Rev.* 131, 2766. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.131.2766](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.131.2766)

name: Classical and quantum non-equilibrium dynamics
summary: Master equations, linear response and fluctuation theorems carry over from classical stochastic systems to open and closed quantum many-body systems. The Lindblad equation is the quantum Markov master equation.

name: KPZ superdiffusion in quantum spin chains
summary: Infinite-temperature spin transport in the isotropic Heisenberg chain is superdiffusive with z=3/2, and the spin profile matches the KPZ scaling function. This was observed with a quantum gas microscope.
breaks: Classical KPZ comes from a noisy, non-integrable growth equation. In the integrable Heisenberg chain the higher moments of the transferred magnetization deviate from Tracy–Widom, so only part of the KPZ phenomenology carries over.
sources: Ljubotina, Žnidarič & Prosen (2019). "Kardar-Parisi-Zhang Physics in the Quantum Heisenberg Magnet". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 122, 210602. [arXiv:1903.01329](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.01329)
Wei et al. (2022). "Quantum gas microscopy of Kardar-Parisi-Zhang superdiffusion". *Science* 376, 716. [arXiv:2107.00038](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.00038)

name: Boundary-driven quantum NESS and matrix products
summary: Boundary-driven Lindblad spin chains are the quantum counterpart of boundary-driven exclusion processes. Their steady states can be solved by matrix-product ansätze like Derrida's ASEP solution, giving exact currents and quantum NESS phase diagrams.
sources: Prosen (2011). "Exact Nonequilibrium Steady State of a Strongly Driven Open XXZ Chain". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 107, 137201. [arXiv:1106.2978](https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.2978)

Derrida et al. (1993). "Exact solution of a 1D asymmetric exclusion model using a matrix formulation". *J. Phys. A* 26, 1493. [doi:10.1088/0305-4470/26/7/011](https://doi.org/10.1088/0305-4470/26/7/011)

name: Transport coefficients from scattering cross sections
summary: The Boltzmann collision integral takes its input from quantum scattering theory: dσ/dΩ fixes the mean free path, and Chapman–Enskog transport cross sections fix viscosity and conductivity. In ultracold gases the s-wave σ=8πa² sets thermalization and evaporative cooling.

name: ETH implies the fluctuation–dissipation theorem
summary: The smooth function f_O(E,ω) in the ETH ansatz fixes both the spectral function and the symmetrized correlator of O. Their ratio is the equilibrium FDT at the temperature of the eigenstate, so single eigenstates satisfy the FDT.
sources: D'Alessio et al. (2016). "From quantum chaos and eigenstate thermalization to statistical mechanics and thermodynamics". *Adv. Phys.* 65, 239. [arXiv:1509.06411](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.06411)

name: Thermal noise and cooling of mechanical oscillators
summary: A mechanical resonator's thermal force noise follows from the FDT applied to its susceptibility, and cavity sideband cooling engineers a colder effective bath. The asymmetry between Stokes and anti-Stokes sidebands (∝ n̄+1 vs n̄) is the quantum FDT, used as a primary thermometer.
sources: Aspelmeyer, Kippenberg & Marquardt (2014). "Cavity optomechanics". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 86, 1391. [arXiv:1303.0733](https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.0733)

name: Quantum FDT and the standard quantum limit
summary: The quantum FDT, with ħω coth(ħω/2k_BT) in place of 2k_BT, gives zero-point noise that sets the standard quantum limit of linear amplifiers and interferometers. Squeezing redistributes this noise between quadratures and cannot remove it.
sources: Callen & Welton (1951). "Irreversibility and Generalized Noise". *Phys. Rev.* 83, 34. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.83.34](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.83.34)
Clerk et al. (2010). "Introduction to quantum noise, measurement, and amplification". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 82, 1155. [arXiv:0810.4729](https://arxiv.org/abs/0810.4729)

name: Doppler cooling as Brownian motion in light
summary: Optical molasses is a Langevin system: radiation pressure provides linear friction and random spontaneous-emission recoils provide momentum diffusion. The Einstein relation k_BT=D_p/α gives the Doppler limit k_BT_D=ħΓ/2.

name: Caldeira–Leggett: quantum Brownian motion
summary: A particle linearly coupled to an Ohmic bath of oscillators obeys the classical Langevin equation at high T, but in quantum form it decoheres spatial superpositions at a rate ∝ γ(Δx/λ_th)². Classical friction and quantum decoherence come from one bath spectral density.
sources: Caldeira & Leggett (1983). "Path integral approach to quantum Brownian motion". *Physica A* 121, 587. [doi:10.1016/0378-4371(83)90013-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/0378-4371(83)90013-4)

name: Lindblad equation as the quantum master equation
summary: The Lindblad equation is the quantum version of the Pauli master equation and Fokker–Planck dynamics. Its diagonal part in the energy basis is a classical rate equation with detailed balance, and quantum trajectories are a stochastic unravelling like Langevin paths.

name: Kramers escape and instanton tunnelling rates
summary: Kramers' thermal escape rate and the Langer–Coleman–Caldeira–Leggett imaginary-time instanton rate are two limits of one rate theory. Below the crossover temperature T_0=ħω_b/2πk_B, macroscopic quantum tunnelling replaces activation, as observed in Josephson junctions.
sources: Hänggi, Talkner & Borkovec (1990). "Reaction-rate theory: fifty years after Kramers". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 62, 251. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.62.251](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.62.251)
Caldeira & Leggett (1983). "Path integral approach to quantum Brownian motion". *Physica A* 121, 587. [doi:10.1016/0378-4371(83)90013-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/0378-4371(83)90013-4)

name: Quantum-jump stochastic thermodynamics
summary: Unravelling Lindblad dynamics into quantum-jump trajectories assigns heat to each emitted or absorbed quantum. Full-counting statistics of these currents obey Gallavotti–Cohen symmetries and TURs (with quantum corrections), mirroring classical stochastic thermodynamics.
sources: Esposito, Harbola & Mukamel (2008). "Nonequilibrium fluctuations, fluctuation theorems, and counting statistics in quantum systems". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 81, 1665. [arXiv:0811.3717](https://arxiv.org/abs/0811.3717)

name: Quantum fluctuation theorems
summary: Jarzynski and Crooks relations hold for closed quantum systems when work is defined by two projective energy measurements. Strong coupling and coherence complicate the definition of heat.
sources: Esposito, Harbola & Mukamel (2008). "Nonequilibrium fluctuations, fluctuation theorems, and counting statistics in quantum systems". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 81, 1665. [arXiv:0811.3717](https://arxiv.org/abs/0811.3717)
Jarzynski (1997). "Nonequilibrium Equality for Free Energy Differences". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 78, 2690. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.78.2690](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.78.2690)

name: Kibble–Zurek measurement of BEC critical exponents
summary: Quenching a homogeneous Bose gas through T_c freezes in defects and coherence domains whose size scales as τ_Q^{ν/(1+zν)}. This measured ν≈0.5 and z≈1.4 in homogeneous gases, and trapped-gas correlation-length measurements gave ν≈0.67 (3D XY).
sources: Navon et al. (2015). "Critical dynamics of spontaneous symmetry breaking in a homogeneous Bose gas". *Science* 347, 167. [arXiv:1410.8487](https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.8487)

name: Entanglement entropy at quantum critical points
summary: At a 1+1D quantum critical point the ground-state entanglement entropy grows as (c/3) ln L, so the central charge that labels the universality class can be read off from entanglement. Gapped phases obey an area law instead.
sources: Calabrese & Cardy (2004). "Entanglement entropy and quantum field theory". *J. Stat. Mech.* P06002. [arXiv:hep-th/0405152](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0405152)
Vidal et al. (2002). "Entanglement in quantum critical phenomena". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 90, 227902. [arXiv:quant-ph/0211074](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0211074)

name: Cold atoms as analog simulators of lattice models
summary: Bose–Hubbard and Fermi–Hubbard models in optical lattices realize lattice models from statistical mechanics with tunable couplings, including the superfluid–Mott transition and antiferromagnetic Ising and Heisenberg correlations. Quantum gas microscopes measure spin correlations site by site.
sources: Greiner et al. (2002). "Quantum phase transition from a superfluid to a Mott insulator in a gas of ultracold atoms". *Nature* 415, 39. [doi:10.1038/415039a](https://doi.org/10.1038/415039a)

name: Rydberg and ion arrays as programmable Ising magnets
summary: Rydberg-blockade tweezer arrays and trapped-ion chains implement transverse-field and long-range Ising models with hundreds of spins. Slow sweeps through their quantum critical points measure Kibble–Zurek scaling, which gives ν and z.
sources: Ebadi et al. (2021). "Quantum phases of matter on a 256-atom programmable quantum simulator". *Nature* 595, 227. [arXiv:2012.12281](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.12281)
Keesling et al. (2019). "Quantum Kibble–Zurek mechanism and critical dynamics on a programmable Rydberg simulator". *Nature* 568, 207. [arXiv:1809.05540](https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.05540)

name: Quantum–classical mapping: TFIM ↔ (d+1)D Ising
summary: Suzuki–Trotter decomposition maps the d-dimensional transverse-field Ising model at T=0 onto an anisotropic (d+1)-dimensional classical Ising model. The quantum critical point therefore sits in the (d+1)D Ising class, with imaginary time acting as an extra dimension and z=1.
map: e^{-\beta H_{TFIM}}\to\prod e^{K_\tau s_{i,\tau}s_{i,\tau+1}+K s_{i,\tau}s_{j,\tau}},\ \tanh K_\tau=e^{-2\Delta\tau\Gamma}
sources: Suzuki (1976). "Relationship between d-Dimensional Quantal Spin Systems and (d+1)-Dimensional Ising Systems". *Prog. Theor. Phys.* 56, 1454. [doi:10.1143/PTP.56.1454](https://doi.org/10.1143/PTP.56.1454)

name: Gross–Pitaevskii and BCS–BEC crossover as mean field
summary: The Gross–Pitaevskii equation is the Hartree mean-field theory of a condensate, with the macroscopic wavefunction as Landau order parameter. For fermions, BCS mean-field theory with a self-consistent chemical potential interpolates from BCS pairs to molecular BEC across a Feshbach resonance.
breaks: GP mean field fails in 1D and near unitarity, where fluctuations and beyond-mean-field (Lee–Huang–Yang) corrections matter.
sources: Dalfovo et al. (1998). "Theory of Bose-Einstein condensation in trapped gases". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 71, 463. [arXiv:cond-mat/9806038](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9806038)

name: Dicke superradiance as an exact mean-field transition
summary: Atoms coupled to one cavity mode interact all-to-all, so the Dicke/Hepp–Lieb superradiant transition is mean-field exact. A BEC in a pumped cavity realized it as self-organization into a checkerboard lattice, an open-system phase transition with a Landau order parameter ⟨a⟩.
sources: Baumann et al. (2010). "Dicke quantum phase transition with a superfluid gas in an optical cavity". *Nature* 464, 1301. [doi:10.1038/nature09009](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature09009)

name: BKT transition in 2D atomic gases
summary: Quasi-2D trapped Bose gases show the BKT transition directly: interference contrast reveals quasi-long-range phase coherence below T_BKT, and free vortices proliferate above it. Uniform-box gases later confirmed the universal superfluid-density jump.
sources: Hadzibabic et al. (2006). "Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless crossover in a trapped atomic gas". *Nature* 441, 1118. [arXiv:cond-mat/0605291](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0605291)

Kosterlitz & Thouless (1973). "Ordering, metastability and phase transitions in two-dimensional systems". *J. Phys. C* 6, 1181. [doi:10.1088/0022-3719/6/7/010](https://doi.org/10.1088/0022-3719/6/7/010)

name: Shared core: the driven two-level atom
summary: Rabi oscillations, optical Bloch equations, dressed states and resonance fluorescence are common to both. AMO uses them to cool, trap and probe atoms; quantum optics uses them to make and characterize non-classical light (antibunching, the Mollow triplet).
sources: Kimble, Dagenais & Mandel (1977). "Photon Antibunching in Resonance Fluorescence". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 39, 691. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.39.691](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.39.691)

name: Quantum-logic spectroscopy: ion QC gates run clocks
summary: Phonon-bus gates developed for trapped-ion quantum computing let a logic ion read out a clock ion that lacks a cycling transition, giving Al+ clocks at the 10^-18 level. Entanglement-enhanced and tweezer-array clocks now also run on quantum-computing hardware.
sources: Cirac & Zoller (1995). "Quantum Computations with Cold Trapped Ions". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 74, 4091. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.74.4091](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.74.4091)
Ludlow et al. (2015). "Optical atomic clocks". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 87, 637. [arXiv:1407.3493](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.3493)

name: Projection noise and spin squeezing in atomic clocks
summary: Ramsey spectroscopy with N uncorrelated atoms is limited by quantum projection noise, the atomic counterpart of photon shot noise in interferometers. Spin-squeezed or entangled atoms, the analogue of injecting squeezed light, push clocks and atom interferometers below the standard quantum limit toward the Heisenberg limit.
breaks: In clocks the local-oscillator noise and Dick effect often dominate over projection noise, so squeezing gains are smaller than ideal.
sources: Caves (1981). "Quantum-mechanical noise in an interferometer". *Phys. Rev. D* 23, 1693. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.23.1693](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.23.1693)
Ludlow et al. (2015). "Optical atomic clocks". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 87, 637. [arXiv:1407.3493](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.3493)

name: Atomic term structure from angular-momentum coupling
summary: Atomic levels are labelled by coupled angular momenta (LS or jj coupling). Clebsch–Gordan algebra and the Wigner–Eckart theorem give the fine and hyperfine intervals, Landé g-factors and electric-dipole selection rules.

name: Exact hydrogen spectrum underpins atomic spectroscopy
summary: The Coulomb problem gives the Bohr levels, with an accidental l-degeneracy from hidden SO(4) symmetry. Fine structure, the Lamb shift and hyperfine splitting are perturbations of this exact spectrum, and quantum defects extend it to alkali Rydberg series.

name: Bosonic Josephson junction vs Cooper-pair box
summary: A condensate in a double well follows a two-mode Bose–Hubbard Hamiltonian that maps onto the junction Hamiltonian behind charge qubits and transmons: number imbalance plays the role of Cooper-pair number and relative phase the role of φ. Josephson plasma oscillations are observed, and ring condensates with weak links form atomtronic SQUIDs.
breaks: Atoms are neutral and conserve total number, so there is no 2e charging, gate charge or electromagnetic environment. Large population imbalance gives nonlinear self-trapping. Large N and slow (Hz–kHz) dynamics mean the atomic junction is not a practical qubit.

name: s-wave scattering length sets condensate interactions
summary: At ultracold energies only s-wave scattering survives, so interactions reduce to a contact pseudopotential g = 4πħ²a/m in the Gross–Pitaevskii equation. Feshbach resonances, a bound-state resonance of partial-wave theory, tune a through zero and infinity, enabling the BEC–BCS crossover and Feshbach molecules.
breaks: The contact pseudopotential fails near resonance, where na³ is not small and three-body losses and effective-range terms matter.
sources: Chin et al. (2010). "Feshbach resonances in ultracold gases". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 82, 1225. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.82.1225](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.82.1225)

name: Quantum trajectories grew out of laser-cooling theory
summary: The optical Bloch equations of a driven two-level atom are the prototype Lindbladian and set the Doppler limit. The Monte Carlo wave-function unraveling (Dalibard, Castin, Mølmer; alongside Carmichael and Zoller's group) was developed in this community, and simulations of sub-Doppler and sub-recoil cooling were among its first uses.

name: Laser cooling and tweezers prepare atomic qubits
summary: Doppler and resolved-sideband cooling bring trapped ions to the motional ground state that phonon-bus gates need. MOT loading and optical tweezers with atom rearrangement assemble defect-free neutral-atom qubit arrays.
sources: Cirac & Zoller (1995). "Quantum Computations with Cold Trapped Ions". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 74, 4091. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.74.4091](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.74.4091)

name: Resolved-sideband cooling of ions and mechanical modes
summary: Red-detuned driving scatters photons mainly into the anti-Stokes sideband, removing one phonon per photon. The same rate-equation theory sets the minimum occupancy of trapped ions and of radiation-pressure-cooled membranes, and levitated nanoparticles in optical tweezers join the two fields.
sources: Marquardt et al. (2007). "Quantum Theory of Cavity-Assisted Sideband Cooling of Mechanical Motion". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 99, 093902. [doi:10.1103/physrevlett.99.093902](https://doi.org/10.1103/physrevlett.99.093902)
Teufel et al. (2011). "Sideband cooling of micromechanical motion to the quantum ground state". *Nature* 475, 359. [doi:10.1038/nature10261](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature10261)

name: Lattice-gas quenches test thermalization and MBL
summary: Bose- and Fermi-Hubbard gases in optical lattices are isolated, tunable many-body systems. Their quench dynamics directly test ETH, prethermalization and many-body localization, which was seen in quasi-periodic lattices.
map: H=-J\sum_{\langle ij\rangle}a_i^\dagger a_j+\tfrac U2\sum_i n_i(n_i-1)+\sum_i\epsilon_i n_i
breaks: Finite size, finite times and residual heating or atom loss stop experiments from settling thermodynamic-limit questions such as whether MBL is stable.
sources: Bloch, Dalibard & Zwerger (2008). "Many-body physics with ultracold gases". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 80, 885. [arXiv:0704.3011](https://arxiv.org/abs/0704.3011)

name: Atom arrays as digital qubits and analog simulators
summary: The same neutral atoms in lattices or tweezer arrays serve as digital qubits, with Rydberg-blockade gates, and as analog simulators of Ising and Hubbard models. Both rely on site-resolved fluorescence imaging, as in quantum-gas microscopes.

name: Synthetic gauge fields and Chern bands for neutral atoms
summary: Neutral atoms gain an artificial vector potential, either as the Berry connection of dressed internal states or as Peierls phases from laser-assisted or shaken-lattice tunnelling. This produced Hofstadter and Haldane Chern bands, whose Berry curvature and Chern numbers are measured from transverse drift and Thouless pumping.
breaks: The fields are engineered through driving, which causes heating, and spontaneous emission limits lifetimes. Without disorder, leads or a Fermi sea they show no clean quantized Hall plateau.
sources: Jotzu et al. (2014). "Experimental realization of the topological Haldane model with ultracold fermions". *Nature* 515, 237. [doi:10.1038/nature13915](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature13915)
Berry (1984). "Quantal phase factors accompanying adiabatic changes". *Proc. R. Soc. A* 392, 45. [doi:10.1098/rspa.1984.0023](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1984.0023)

name: Bell violation certifies entanglement
summary: Any violation of a Bell inequality certifies entanglement without trusting the devices, and the Tsirelson bound caps the quantum value. The converse fails: some entangled states, such as certain Werner states, admit local hidden-variable models, so nonlocality and entanglement are distinct resources.
sources: Horodecki et al. (2009). "Quantum entanglement". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 81, 865. [arXiv:quant-ph/0702225](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0702225)

name: Bell violation as a security certificate (E91, DI-QKD)
summary: Ekert's protocol uses a CHSH violation to bound an eavesdropper's information. Device-independent QKD and certified randomness turn loophole-free Bell tests into security proofs that do not trust the hardware.
sources: Ekert (1991). "Quantum cryptography based on Bell's theorem". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 67, 661. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.67.661](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.67.661)
Hensen et al. (2015). "Loophole-free Bell inequality violation using electron spins separated by 1.3 kilometres". *Nature* 526, 682. [arXiv:1508.05949](https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.05949)

name: Contextuality as the resource behind quantum speedup
summary: Clifford circuits on stabilizer states are classically simulable (Gottesman–Knill); universality comes from injecting magic states. For odd-prime-dimensional qudits, contextuality is necessary for magic-state universality; for qubits the link is subtler.
breaks: For qubits, state-independent contextuality already exists within the classically simulable stabilizer theory, so contextuality is not a clean sufficient marker there.

name: Lindblad dephasing is the dynamics of decoherence
summary: Tracing out the environment under the Born–Markov approximation gives a Lindblad equation. Its dephasing term damps coherences between pointer states exponentially, at a rate set by their separation, which quantifies einselection.
breaks: Non-Markovian or strongly coupled environments give decoherence that is not of Lindblad form, with memory effects and coherence revivals.
sources: Zurek (2003). "Decoherence, einselection, and the quantum origins of the classical". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 75, 715. [arXiv:quant-ph/0105127](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0105127)
Lindblad (1976). "On the generators of quantum dynamical semigroups". *Commun. Math. Phys.* 48, 119. [doi:10.1007/BF01608499](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01608499)

name: Error correction and DFS undo decoherence
summary: Error correction treats decoherence as a channel with Kraus operators E_k and recovers the encoded state when the Knill–Laflamme conditions hold. Collective environment coupling gives decoherence-free subspaces, the passive limit of the same algebra, where protected code spaces replace pointer states.

name: Qubit T1 and T2 as measured decoherence
summary: Superconducting circuits are macroscopic quantum systems whose coherence is limited by TLS defects, quasiparticles, and flux and charge noise, so T1/T2 measurements and noise spectroscopy are direct studies of decoherence. The transmon design suppresses charge-noise dephasing exponentially.
sources: Koch et al. (2007). "Charge-insensitive qubit design derived from the Cooper pair box". *Phys. Rev. A* 76, 042319. [arXiv:cond-mat/0703002](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0703002)

name: Influence functional and Caldeira–Leggett decoherence
summary: Integrating a harmonic bath out of the path integral gives the Feynman–Vernon influence functional. For an ohmic bath at high temperature this yields the Caldeira–Leggett master equation and the standard estimate that a superposition of separation Δx decoheres faster than it relaxes by a factor (Δx/λ_th)².
breaks: Valid only for high temperature and ohmic, Markovian baths. At low temperature the master equation is not of Lindblad form and needs corrections.
sources: Caldeira & Leggett (1983). "Quantum tunnelling in a dissipative system". *Ann. Phys.* 149, 374. [doi:10.1016/0003-4916(83)90202-6](https://doi.org/10.1016/0003-4916(83)90202-6)
Zurek (2003). "Decoherence, einselection, and the quantum origins of the classical". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 75, 715. [arXiv:quant-ph/0105127](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0105127)
